Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Ravikant Patidar, learned P.L. for the respondent/State.
Heard.

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 0197/2019 registered at Police Station Industrial Area Satlapur, district Raisen (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 272, 273 and 420 of IPC.

As per prosecution case in short is that on 08.08.2019, Food Safety Officer, Raisen has filed an application before police Station Industrial Area Satlapur stating that under instruction of Collector,
on 27.07.2019, complainant along with members of constituted inquiry committee went to M/s National Industries for inspection.
The inquiry officers have taken samples of ghee, butter, milk powder and pulp of custard apple (sheetafal).
On examination, the sample of ghee is found below standard.

It is further contended in application that Collector has directed to register the case against the applicant and Supervisor of Industry for the offences under Sections 272, 273 and 420 of IPC in addition to provision of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
The co-accused Ganesh Yadav has already been granted the regular bail by the Lower Court.

The offences under Section 272 and 273 of IPC, alleged against the applicant are non cognizable, thus, to bring the case of applicant under the category of cognizance offence, the authority has wrongly inserted the offence of Section 420 of IPC.
The applicant has not committed any cheating with anyone and 2 MCRC-39678-2019 non of private person has made any complaint against the applicant.
The ingredients of cheating is not fulfilled.

For the sake of argument, if it is assumed that the product of the applicant are sub standard then same is to be dealt under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text: Per - contra, learned P.L. for the respondent/State opposes the anticipatory bail application.
Heard both the parties and perused the case diary.

On perusal of case diary, it seems that on the complaint of Food 3 MCRC-39678-2019 Safety Officer,
Raisen, Police has registered the FIR against the applicant and co-accused/Ganesh Yadav.
Applicant has also filed the order dated 26.08.2019 by which the learned Lower Court has allowed the application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed by co-accused/Ganesh Yadav.

The allegation against the present applicant is that the sample of Ghee taken by Inquiry Officer from his Industry is found sub-standard, thus, offences of Sections 272, 273 and 420 has been registered against the present applicant.

Under the provision of Section 51 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, there is also penalty prescribed for manufacturing for sell, selling store, distribute and imports of any sub-standard articles of food.
The offences of Section 272 and 273 of IPC are non-cognizable.

After considering the arguments of applicant's counsel and looking to the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, this Court is of the opinion that applicant-Rajesh Gupta is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this application for anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicant-Rajesh Gupta is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of his arrest, the applicant shall be released on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) and a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before the trial Court on all dates and for complying with the conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of section 438 of the Rajesh Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182572831/
